answer: A walnut earns its dates the way wood earns history: rings alone prove nothing, only cross-dating against a master chronology built from many independent trees makes a year real. Copy a parent's ring pattern and the lab names you: identical rings are one tree, not two; a farm is photocopies under one bark. Trust is pigment soaked into public wood like walnut-husk dye that never lifts: every sealed grade and attestation stains, no repainting later. The ridge of the network's history is shared stone; chisel one verifiable groove and let the whole forest date you.
